project.title: 面向飞机 B-Rep 模型小特征处理的可追溯图学习与几何重建框架
project.target_venue: Journal of Computational Design and Engineering (provisional)

artifacts.path: ../飞机STEP模型小特征识别期刊论文逻辑大纲_按意见修订_最终版.docx

contract.gap: Existing CAD feature-recognition work provides limited evidence for traceable, risk-sensitive small-feature recognition and downstream geometry processing on complete heterogeneous aircraft B-Rep models.
contract.task: Recognize rivets and other surface features at B-Rep face level, preserve STEP face traceability, and validate safety-aware downstream CAD removal and reconstruction.
outcomes: per-aircraft error and background false-positive analysis
traceable CAD removal and geometry reconstruction
optional mesh and CAE impact validation

questions.text: Can face geometry and adjacency topology support rivet and surface-feature recognition across complete aircraft models?
Does independent dual-specialist encoding reduce task interference relative to a unified classifier?
Can smooth-shell protection reduce high-risk background false positives without unacceptable true-feature loss?
Can predictions remain traceable to STEP faces and support auditable geometry removal and reconstruction?

contract.contribution: A traceable, risk-sensitive graph-learning and CAD geometry-processing framework for small features in complete aircraft B-Rep models.
nonclaims: No universal generalization claim across all aircraft or CAD sources.
BRep validity alone does not establish geometry or physics equivalence.
No CAE acceleration or response-preservation claim before controlled downstream experiments.
Human visual review is not described as fully automatic validation.
Retired BFS and 51-dimensional experiments are not part of the formal model.

semantic_locks.canonical: background=0, rivet=1, surface_feature=2; decal and window provenance remains in JSON
Dataset partitioning is performed by complete aircraft model, not by randomly splitting faces
Do not use a 0.0005 normalized-area hard prediction filter because valid large surface features exist

style_profile.language_variant: US English for manuscript; Simplified Chinese for planning

facts.value: 48 node features, 6 edge attributes, 4 layers, hidden dimension 64, seed 123, 50 epochs, rivet threshold 0.9, surface threshold 0.5

alignment.method: B-Rep face graph with geometric and topological attributes
alignment.evidence: Frozen complete-aircraft evaluation and STEP overlays

alignment.method: Dual-specialist GNN versus unified three-class baseline
alignment.limitation: Architecture and parameter-count fairness must be documented

alignment.method: Raw prediction versus area filter versus smooth-shell guard
alignment.evidence: Per-aircraft FP, maximum FP area, and true-positive loss
alignment.limitation: Guard parameters may be domain dependent

alignment.method: face_id traceability, CAD removal, local reconstruction, and BRep checks
alignment.evidence: Nine final STEP models plus quantitative geometry validation
alignment.result: Final STEP models exist; unified quantitative table pending
alignment.limitation: BRep validity does not prove physical equivalence

decisions.decision: Plan the paper as an end-to-end recognition and geometry-processing framework, with a recognition-only fallback title if downstream evidence remains insufficient.
Treat the 3631-face evaluation as historical because it does not match the current 34156-face candidate test CSV.
